books.title: 504 Absolutely Essential Words
books.author: Murray Bromberg · Julius Liebb · Arthur Traiger
books.about_en: The classic word list every learner meets first: twelve words a lesson, each with a meaning, a plain definition and sentences that show it working.
books.about_fa: فهرست کلاسیک واژه‌ها؛ در هر درس دوازده واژه، با معنی، تعریف ساده و چند جمله که کاربردش را نشان می‌دهد.

words.def_en: to leave someone or something behind for good, with no plan to come back
examples: They abandoned the car when the road flooded.
She abandoned her plan to study law after one term.

words.def_en: very eager to do something; or sharp, as a mind, an eye or a sense
examples: He is keen to start his new job.
A keen eye will notice the small difference.

words.def_en: unhappy because someone has what you want, or afraid of losing someone you love
examples: He was jealous of his brother's new bike.
She felt jealous when her friend was chosen instead of her.

words.def_en: the skill of saying a difficult thing without upsetting the person who hears it
examples: She told him about the mistake with great tact.
A teacher needs tact as much as knowledge.

words.def_en: a formal promise, often made before a judge, that what you say is true
examples: The witness took an oath before speaking.
He broke his oath and lost their trust.

words.def_en: empty; not occupied by anyone, or not being used
examples: The seat next to me was vacant.
They moved into a vacant office on the second floor.

words.def_en: serious difficulty and suffering, usually over a long time
examples: The family faced years of hardship after the factory closed.
She never forgot the hardships of her first winter there.

words.def_en: brave and polite, especially towards someone in danger or in need of help
examples: A gallant young officer carried the child out of the fire.
His gallant attempt to save the boat was praised by everyone.

words.def_en: facts and numbers collected so that they can be studied
examples: The data show that the new method works.
We collected data from two hundred students.

words.def_en: not used to something, so that it feels strange to you
examples: He was unaccustomed to speaking in public.
Her eyes were unaccustomed to the bright light.

words.def_en: an unmarried man; also the first university degree
examples: My uncle stayed a bachelor until he was forty.
She finished her bachelor's degree last spring.

words.def_en: to reach the standard that a job, a course or a competition asks for
examples: He qualified as a doctor after six years.
Only two runners qualified for the final.

words.def_en: dark, dull and depressing, as a place, the weather or a mood can be
examples: The room looked dismal after the storm.
It was a dismal morning, grey from the first light.

words.def_en: to risk money on the result of a game or an event
examples: He wagered ten dollars on the last race.
She wagered her brother that the train would be late.

words.def_en: serious danger, the kind that can harm or kill
examples: The sailors were in peril when the storm struck.
He set out in the snow, blind to the peril ahead.

words.def_en: to lie back or lean back in a relaxed position
examples: She reclined on the sofa and closed her eyes.
The seat reclines almost flat for sleeping.

words.def_en: to give a loud, high cry, from fear or delight
examples: The children shrieked with delight in the water.
We heard a shriek from the garden and ran out.

words.def_en: seeming evil, dishonest or threatening without saying so plainly
examples: There was something sinister about the empty house.
The letter carried a sinister warning.

words.def_en: to hide something carefully so that it cannot be seen or found
examples: He concealed the key under a loose stone.
She could not conceal her disappointment.

words.def_en: to live in a place, as people or animals do
examples: Few animals inhabit the desert.
The old house is no longer inhabited.

words.def_en: extremely cold; also unfriendly in manner
examples: A frigid wind came off the lake.
She gave him a frigid look and walked on.

words.def_en: unable to feel or move a part of the body, from cold or shock
examples: My fingers were numb with cold.
The injection made his arm go numb.

words.def_en: the body of a dead person or animal
examples: The police found a corpse beside the river.
A corpse lay under a sheet on the ground.

words.def_en: to make someone want something, often something they should not have
examples: The smell of fresh bread tempted me into the shop.
Do not tempt him with offers he cannot refuse.

words.def_en: happening once every year, or calculated over one year
examples: The company holds an annual meeting in June.
Her annual income rose a little last year.

words.def_en: to mix two or more things so that they become one
examples: Blend the flour and butter together.
The tea is blended from three kinds of leaf.

words.def_en: the smallest amount that is possible or allowed
examples: We keep the cost to a minimum.
The minimum for the course is two hours a week.

words.def_en: a natural ability to do something well
examples: She has a talent for explaining difficult ideas.
The choir is full of young talent.

words.def_en: to make someone agree to do something by giving them reasons
examples: He persuaded his brother to lend him the car.
I was persuaded by her argument.

words.def_en: able to be seen, or easy to notice
examples: The mountain is visible from our window.
There was a visible change in his face.

words.def_en: showing the usual qualities of a person, place or thing
examples: It was a typical winter morning, cold and grey.
That answer is typical of him.

words.def_en: to think of a plan, method or tool that did not exist before
examples: They devised a cheap way to filter the water.
She devised a plan to finish the work in a week.

words.def_en: completely necessary, so that something cannot work without it
examples: Water is essential for life.
It is essential to check the figures twice.

words.def_en: sold in large amounts to shops, which then sell it to others
examples: He buys the fruit at wholesale prices.
The wholesale market opens before dawn.

words.def_en: not available in enough quantity for everyone who needs it
examples: Clean water is scarce in the region.
Tickets were scarce, so we bought them early.

words.def_en: costing a lot of money
examples: That restaurant is too expensive for a weeknight.
Repairing the roof was expensive.

words.def_en: having a lot of water in the air, so that the heat feels heavy
examples: The kitchen was hot and humid.
Summer here is humid from morning to night.

words.def_en: to disappear suddenly, often without a sign
examples: The keys vanished from the table.
He vanished into the crowd.

words.def_en: packed closely together, so that air or light hardly gets through
examples: A dense fog covered the road.
The forest here is very dense.

words.def_en: to say what you think will happen before it happens
examples: Nobody can predict the weather a month ahead.
They predicted a heavy harvest this year.

words.def_en: the bad character in a story, or a person who does evil
examples: The villain of the novel is never named.
He played the villain and enjoyed every minute.

words.def_en: the gas that a liquid becomes when it is heated
examples: Vapor rose from the boiling pot.
In cold air the vapor of your breath shows white.

words.def_en: extremely large in size or amount
examples: An enormous tree stood in the garden.
The project cost an enormous amount of money.

words.def_en: an idea or set of ideas offered to explain something
examples: Darwin's theory changed biology.
In theory the plan works, but nobody has tried it.

words.def_en: to use something in a practical way, especially a resource
examples: The farm utilizes every drop of rain water.
We utilized the space under the stairs.

words.def_en: to go down from a higher place to a lower one
examples: The plane began to descend toward the runway.
We descended the stairs in the dark.

words.def_en: to remove something completely, or to take a team out of a contest
examples: The new rules eliminate most paperwork.
They were eliminated in the first round.

words.def_en: to move around a system or a group, as air or news does
examples: Warm air circulates through the room.
The story circulated for a week before anyone denied it.

words.def_en: belonging to the countryside rather than a town
examples: The clinic serves five rural villages.
He grew up in a rural area with no bus service.

words.def_en: the land and buildings of a university or a large school
examples: The library stands in the middle of the campus.
Students live on campus in the first year.

words.def_en: to escape something by doing it in a clever, indirect way
examples: He evaded the question with a joke.
The boat evaded the police and left the harbour.

words.def_en: the larger part of a group, more than half the people
examples: The majority of the class chose the earlier time.
She won by a large majority.

words.def_en: to bring people together, or to put the parts of something together
examples: The whole staff assembled in the hall.
It took an hour to assemble the new shelves.

words.def_en: a habit or custom passed down through the years in a family or people
examples: It is a tradition to eat fish on that night.
The school keeps the tradition alive.

words.def_en: a heavy load of work, worry or cost that a person must carry
examples: The cost became a burden on the family.
He carried the burden of the debt alone.

words.def_en: to travel through a place to find out about it, or to examine an idea
examples: They explored the caves north of the town.
We should explore every option before deciding.

words.def_en: a change made to improve a law, a system or an institution
examples: The tax reform helped small businesses.
He spent his life calling for education reforms.

words.def_en: the subject that a talk, a lesson or a piece of writing is about
examples: The topic of the lesson was food.
We changed the topic before it turned into an argument.

words.def_en: to ask careful questions or look closely into something hidden
examples: The reporter probed the reasons for the delay.
Doctors probed the wound to see how deep it was.

words.def_en: a formal discussion in which people give opposing reasons
examples: The debate about the road lasted three hours.
She spoke well in the class debate.

words.def_en: complete, with nothing missed out
examples: The mechanic gave the car a thorough check.
She made a thorough study of the case.

words.def_en: without any doubt at all
examples: Undoubtedly the best film of the year.
He is undoubtedly the strongest player here.

words.def_en: to come near to someone or something, or to begin to deal with a problem
examples: A stranger approached me at the station.
They approached the problem in a new way.

words.def_en: liked by a lot of people
examples: She is popular with her students.
That song was popular for years.

words.def_en: to fail to give care or attention to something
examples: He neglected his health for years.
The garden was neglected all summer.

words.def_en: a person who is paid to work for a company
examples: Every employee gets a badge.
The company hired fifty new employees.

words.def_en: a fault in something that makes it less than perfect
examples: The car was returned because of a defect in the brakes.
Tests found no defect in the steel.

words.def_en: to make someone believe something that is not true
examples: He deceived the buyer with a false document.
Do not let the price deceive you.

words.def_en: to take money from someone by cheating them
examples: They defrauded the bank of two million.
He was jailed for defrauding elderly clients.

words.def_en: to notice or find something that is not easy to see
examples: The alarm detects smoke within seconds.
Nobody detected the mistake until March.

words.def_en: a person who pays for a service or for advice
examples: The lawyer called his client back.
Our clients expect a quick answer.

words.def_en: including everything that is needed
examples: The report is comprehensive and easy to read.
She gave a comprehensive account of the trip.

words.def_en: to keep something in good condition over time
examples: Salt was used to preserve the fish.
The town has preserved its old houses.

words.def_en: dark and sad, or without hope
examples: The room was gloomy after the sun went down.
He looked gloomy when he heard the news.

words.def_en: permission given by someone who is able to refuse
examples: She gave her consent to the operation.
The work cannot begin without your consent.

words.def_en: being the only one of its kind
examples: Every fingerprint is unique.
The village has a unique charm.

words.def_en: to feel angry about something you think is unfair
examples: She resented the extra work.
He resented being called a beginner.

words.def_en: to say publicly that something is wrong or evil
examples: The council denounced the plan as dangerous.
They denounced the attack in strong words.

words.def_en: to attack or touch someone in a way that harms or frightens them
examples: The dog will not molest anyone who stays calm.
He was accused of molesting a neighbour.

words.def_en: not expected, so not prepared for
examples: The delay was caused by unforeseen problems.
We kept some money for unforeseen costs.

words.def_en: a fast, heavy flow of water, or a stream of words
examples: A torrent of water came down the hill.
She let out a torrent of complaints.

words.def_en: to move something to a later time
examples: We postponed the match until Sunday.
The meeting was postponed twice.

words.def_en: a small closed case, often one you swallow
examples: Take one capsule with water.
The crew sat inside a small capsule.

words.def_en: very large and heavy
examples: A massive rock blocked the road.
The storm caused massive damage.

words.def_en: strange in a way that is hard to explain
examples: A weird noise came from the attic.
It is weird that nobody called.

words.def_en: based on truth or on the rules, so it cannot be refused
examples: Your ticket is valid for one month.
That is a valid reason to be late.

words.def_en: easy to see or understand
examples: The answer was obvious to everyone.
There was an obvious mistake in the first line.

words.def_en: only of average quality, not good
examples: The food was mediocre and cold.
He gave a mediocre performance.

words.def_en: not willing to do something
examples: She was reluctant to lend the car.
He gave a reluctant smile.

words.def_en: to make something seem bigger or worse than it is
examples: Do not exaggerate the danger.
He exaggerated the size of the fish.

words.def_en: safety from danger, or the people and systems that keep it
examples: Security at the airport was slow.
The building has good security.

words.def_en: large and difficult to carry or wear
examples: The parcel was bulky but light.
He wore a bulky winter coat.

words.def_en: someone who does something for pleasure, not as a job
examples: The match was open to amateurs.
He is an amateur photographer.

words.def_en: a collection of different kinds of the same thing
examples: The shop sells a variety of breads.
Her work shows great variety.

words.def_en: important and well known, or easy to see
examples: She is a prominent doctor in the city.
The tower is prominent on the skyline.

words.fa: زنده ماندن، جان به در بردن
words.def_en: to stay alive or to continue after something hard
examples: Two passengers survived the crash.
The old bridge survived the flood.

words.def_en: the area near a place
examples: There is a school in the vicinity.
Police searched the vicinity of the station.

words.def_en: a paper or file that records information
examples: Keep all your documents in one folder.
The document was signed in June.

words.def_en: a period of one hundred years
examples: The church was built in the last century.
A century of rain has worn the stones.

words.def_en: to decide something after thinking, or to end something
examples: We concluded that the plan would fail.
He concluded his talk with a joke.

words.def_en: clearly true, so that nobody can deny it
examples: There is undeniable proof of the change.
Her talent is undeniable.

words.def_en: to fight against something, or to stop yourself doing something
examples: The bridge resisted the flood.
I could not resist the cake.

words.def_en: the state of not having something, or not having enough of it
examples: The plants died from lack of water.
There is no lack of ideas here.

words.def_en: to pay no attention to something on purpose
examples: He ignored my question and left.
Do not ignore the warning light.

words.def_en: something difficult that tests your ability
examples: The climb was a real challenge.
She enjoys the challenge of a new language.

words.def_en: made as a very small copy of something
examples: He builds miniature trains.
A miniature village stood on the table.

words.def_en: the place something comes from
examples: The river is a source of drinking water.
The newspaper would not name its source.

words.def_en: very strong anger that is hard to control
examples: He was shaking with rage.
The rage in her voice surprised us.

words.def_en: to be very good at something, better than others
examples: She excels at mathematics.
He excelled in every sport he tried.

words.def_en: having the qualities people expect of women
examples: The room had a feminine touch.
That name sounds feminine in English.

words.def_en: to climb onto something, or to grow in size or amount
examples: He mounted the horse in one movement.
Pressure mounted on the manager.

words.def_en: to try to win against others
examples: Ten teams competed for the cup.
Small shops compete with the big chains.

words.def_en: to fear something that is going to happen
examples: She dreaded the phone call.
I dread the winter every year.

words.def_en: having the qualities people expect of men
examples: The voice on the phone was masculine.
It is a very masculine style of writing.

words.def_en: a person or thing that is likely to cause harm
examples: The dog was a menace to the postman.
Drunk drivers are a menace on the road.

words.def_en: a habit of behaving in a particular way
examples: He has a tendency to arrive late.
There is a tendency for prices to rise in spring.

words.def_en: to think something is smaller or weaker than it really is
examples: Never underestimate the power of a short walk.
They underestimated the cost by half.

words.def_en: having won a game, a fight or a competition
examples: The victorious team came home at dawn.
She left the court victorious.

words.def_en: existing in large numbers
examples: There were numerous complaints about the noise.
He has written numerous short stories.

words.def_en: able to bend, or able to change to suit new needs
examples: The hose is flexible and easy to store.
We keep flexible hours at work.

books.title: 1100 Words You Need to Know
books.author: Murray Bromberg & Melvin Gordon
books.about_fa: برنامه‌ی هفتگی واژگان برای آمادگی آزمون‌های پیشرفته: هر هفته چند روز و هر روز پنج واژه. درس‌ها اکنون از هفته‌ی ۱ آغاز می‌شوند.

words.def_en: wanting or eating very large amounts
examples: She is a voracious reader of history.
The puppies had voracious appetites.

words.def_en: done without choosing carefully, so good and bad are mixed
examples: The bombing was indiscriminate and killed civilians.
His reading was indiscriminate, but wide.

words.def_en: famous and respected in a particular field
examples: An eminent lawyer took the case.
She became an eminent surgeon.

words.def_en: deeply filled or soaked with something, often an idea
examples: He is steeped in the literature of the period.
The town is steeped in old stories.

words.def_en: completely full or well supplied with something
examples: The shelves are replete with rare books.
The evening was replete with good food and talk.

words.def_en: to exist in very large numbers
examples: Wild flowers abound in these hills.
Rumours abound about the new manager.

words.def_en: the use of science in machines and systems that do practical work
examples: Modern technology has changed farming.
The school invested in new technology.

words.def_en: to say what will happen in the future
examples: The paper prognosticates a cold winter.
Nobody can prognosticate the result of the election.

words.def_en: a machine that moves by itself, or someone who acts mechanically
examples: The automaton lifted its arm and bowed.
He worked like an automaton for ten hours.

words.fa: زن سالخورده و موقر؛ مدیر داخلی
words.def_en: an older married woman, often one in charge of a household or a school
examples: The matron of the house welcomed us.
A strict matron ran the dormitory.

words.def_en: a statement or situation that seems to contradict itself
examples: It is a paradox that the richest country has hungry children.
The paradox of his story is its truth.

words.def_en: a kingdom, or a field of activity or knowledge
examples: The idea belongs to the realm of science fiction.
The kingdom was a peaceful realm for a century.

words.def_en: the written record of events, year by year
examples: His name is in the annals of the club.
That storm is written in the annals of the town.

words.def_en: something made of two or more parts put together
examples: Salt is a simple compound of sodium and chlorine.
The yard is a compound of three buildings.

words.def_en: a small amount of a colour or of a feeling
examples: There is a tinge of sadness in her voice.
The sky had a tinge of pink.

words.def_en: to keep asking or bothering someone until they agree
examples: The children badgered me for a second story.
Stop badgering the manager about the bill.

words.def_en: to beg someone urgently and emotionally
examples: She implored him to stay in touch.
He implored the court to be patient.

words.def_en: dull, hard work with no interest in it
examples: Housework was pure drudgery for him.
The machine took the drudgery out of the job.

words.def_en: so long that it seems to have no end
examples: The interminable wait ended at midnight.
We sat through an interminable speech.

words.def_en: to notice something, or to understand it in a particular way
examples: He perceived a change in her tone.
The problem is perceived as a threat.
